title: wrap roxygen template for YAML source
description:
In several functions, I have documentation that looks like this: 

> This field is not available in all output formats; it is available in `pdf_document()`, `html_document()`, `word_document()`, `odt_document()`, and `powerpoint_presentation()` by default.

It may be good to refactor this as a roxygen template function eventually to make editing this easier. It's also possible a registry system (as in #16) could be used to generate this automatically

title: Refactor yml prep pattern
description:
In the next release, I'd like to refactor a common pattern to use a function so it's easier to maintain. Most YAML functions look, more or less, like this:

```r
yml_function <- function(
  .yml,
  args = yml_blank()
) {
  yaml_list <- list(
      args = args
  )

  yaml_list <- purrr::discard(yaml_list, is_yml_blank)

  warn_if_duplicate_fields(.yml, yaml_list)
  .yml[names(yaml_list)] <- yaml_list

  .yml
}
```

Most of the second half can be refactored, and there's probably a way to streamline the lists for functions that use entirely top-level fields, as well

title: Blogdown improvements
description:
* `blogdown_archetypes()` is only looking in the theme folder. It needs to search the user's `archetype` folder first, then prioritize any there

title: Feature request: piping to assemble documents.
description:
Just an Idea and not sure how feasible it would be. 

My suggestion is have another function called `body_text()` with the idea that you can pipe all your normal YAML like this: 

```
Year<-2019
YAML<-yml() %>% 
	yml_title(title=paste(Year,"report")) %>% 
	yml_output(html_document(), pdf_document()) 
```
but then have it that you could build the rest of the document by continuing to pipe eg: 

```
report<-YAML %>% 
body_text("#Introduction
		   Welcome to the 2019 final report...") %>% 
	code_chunk({plot(x=1:10, y=1:10) },
			     chunk_name = "plot_1", 	
			     chunk_args=list(fig.width=10, fig.height=10)) %>% 
	body_text("now that we can see some dots lets write the rest of the report")

use_rmarkdown(Report, path = "report.rmd")
```

I a just not entirely sure how you would tell it which bit goes into the YAML and which in the code chunk/ body parts of options if I understand how it would work

title: Adding parameters modifies logical values
description:
I'm trying to create a template `_output.yml` and then allow the user to add certain parameters. However, this modifies the logical values (e.g. true -> yes) because the initial yaml was created with `ymlthis::use_output_yml()` and subsequent modification uses `yaml::write_yaml()`. My modified `output_yml` object no longer nests the entire yaml under `output:` so I cannot use `ymlthis::use_output_yml()`. Is there a more robust way to handle this workflow without calling `ymlthis::yml_output()` again with all the original parameters? 
``` r
output_yml <- ymlthis::yml_output(
  .yml = ymlthis::yml_empty(),
  bookdown::gitbook(
    lib_dir = "assets",
    split_by = "chapter",
    config = list(download = "pdf")
  ),
  bookdown::pdf_book(
    keep_tex = TRUE,
    includes = ymlthis::includes2(in_header = "preamble.tex")
  )
)
print(output_yml)
#> ---
#> output:
#>   bookdown::gitbook:
#>     lib_dir: assets
#>     split_by: chapter
#>     config:
#>       download: pdf
#>   bookdown::pdf_book:
#>     keep_tex: true
#>     includes:
#>       in_header: preamble.tex
#> ---
options(ymlthis.remove_blank_line = TRUE)
ymlthis::use_output_yml(.yml = output_yml, path = tempdir(), quiet = TRUE)
options(ymlthis.remove_blank_line = FALSE)
tmpyml <- file.path(tempdir(), "_output.yml")
# The TRUE values are "true"
readLines(tmpyml)
#> [1] "bookdown::gitbook:"          "  lib_dir: assets"          
#> [3] "  split_by: chapter"         "  config:"                  
#> [5] "    download: pdf"           "bookdown::pdf_book:"        
#> [7] "  keep_tex: true"            "  includes:"                
#> [9] "    in_header: preamble.tex"

output_yml <- yaml::read_yaml(tmpyml)
bib_opts <- list(citation_package = "natbib", toc_bib = TRUE)
output_yml[["bookdown::pdf_book"]] <-
  c(output_yml[["bookdown::pdf_book"]], bib_opts)
ymlthis::as_yml(output_yml)
#> ---
#> bookdown::gitbook:
#>   lib_dir: assets
#>   split_by: chapter
#>   config:
#>     download: pdf
#> bookdown::pdf_book:
#>   keep_tex: true
#>   includes:
#>     in_header: preamble.tex
#>   citation_package: natbib
#>   toc_bib: true
#> ---
yaml::write_yaml(x = output_yml, file = tmpyml)
# The TRUE values are "yes"
readLines(tmpyml)
#>  [1] "bookdown::gitbook:"          "  lib_dir: assets"          
#>  [3] "  split_by: chapter"         "  config:"                  
#>  [5] "    download: pdf"           "bookdown::pdf_book:"        
#>  [7] "  keep_tex: yes"             "  includes:"                
#>  [9] "    in_header: preamble.tex" "  citation_package: natbib" 
#> [11] "  toc_bib: yes"
```

title: use_rmarkdown(): force overwrite existing file (non-interactive mode)
description:
Hello all, 

How could it be be possible to let ```ymlthis``` overwrite an existing file and therefore updating it, using the ```use_rmarkdown()``` function?

I tested it but the prompt (asking for different numbers just for overwriting my temporary file) is a big drawback:
```
Overwrite pre-existing file 'new_written_file.rmd'?

1: I agree
2: Negative
3: Absolutely not

Auswahl: 1
✔ Writing 'new_written_file.rmd'
>
```


I've read, that this means I'm running R in the  interactive mode, and I should go for a script to be non-interactive (batch) mode. 
So I have completed a working shell script running R, but still, the overwriting of files is not possible - no prompt, this time justt stating 
```
> ✔ Leaving 'new_written_file.rmd' unchanged
```

I have basic settings like this for the bash script executing R:
```sh
Rscript -e "
```
```r
require(rmarkdown);
require(magrittr);
require(ymlthis);


# 
temp1= 'new_written_file.rmd';
mytemplate= 'the_template_which_has_some_yaml_to_extract.rmd';
themarkdownfile='myactualfile.rmd;

x <- yml() %>% ## I do this only to make sure the yaml is not interfered
yml_discard(c('author', 'date' ));

# Here starts the problem:
use_rmarkdown(
  .yml = x,
  path = temp1,
  template = mytemplate,
  include_yaml = TRUE,
  include_body = FALSE,
  body = NULL,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  quiet = FALSE);

# Usually works if the file is new, but now the following:

use_rmarkdown(
  path = temp1,
  template = themarkdownfile
  include_yaml = TRUE,
  include_body = TRUE,
  body = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE);

#> ✔ Leaving 'new_written_file.rmd' unchanged
"
# … The file is not written :'(
```
I've tried something like  ``` overwrite = TRUE, ```...  ```open_doc= FALSE``` or ```interactive(FALSE)```, or ```non-interactive()``` …… But I have no solution.. 

If I am doing it interactively, I have to type in a different number all the time for the prompt for the overwriting of the file, here called ```temp1```. So it works very nice in interactive mode, but I want to have it generated automatically, as part of a complex script.

I really hope the answer would simply be setting a hidden option in:
```r
use_rmarkdown(
  open_doc = interactive()
)
```
? 

But I have not yet found an answer. I wish, someone with some experience using R, could give me a hint or even solution?

Kind regards :)

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

title: yml_blank() causes empty list
description:
The default for all of the parameters for `yml_distill_author` are `yml_blank()`, but this causes the yaml to be `author: []`.

Here's a reprex:

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(ymlthis)

# A basic setup
myyml <- yml() %>%
  yml_title("A sample title") %>%
  yml_output(distill::distill_article())

# Only want to add name and affiliation
myyml %>%
  yml_distill_author(name = "John Doe",
                     affiliation = "My Uni")
#> ---
#> author: []
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> title: A sample title
#> output: distill::distill_article
#> ---

# But it works if I add the other params
myyml %>%
  yml_distill_author(
    name = "John Doe",
    url = "url",
    affiliation = "My Uni",
    affiliation_url = "Affil URL",
    orcid_id = "Orcid"
  )
#> ---
#> author:
#> - name: John Doe
#>   affiliation: My Uni
#>   url: url
#>   affiliation_url: Affil URL
#>   orcid_id: Orcid
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> title: A sample title
#> output: distill::distill_article
#> ---

# And providing NULL instead of 'yml_blank` works
myyml %>%
  yml_distill_author(
    name = "John Doe",
    url = "url",
    affiliation = "My Uni",
    affiliation_url = "Affil URL",
    orcid_id = NULL
  )
#> ---
#> author:
#> - name: John Doe
#>   affiliation: My Uni
#>   url: url
#>   affiliation_url: Affil URL
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> title: A sample title
#> output: distill::distill_article
#> ---

# check if the issue is with `yml_blank`
myyml %>%
  yml_author( # Not distill anymore
    name = "John Doe",
    affiliation = yml_blank()
  )
#> ---
#> author: []
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> title: A sample title
#> output: distill::distill_article
#> ---
```

<sup>Created on 2021-09-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Seems like maybe the solution is for `yml_distill_author` to use `NULL` as the default. That would make it the same as `yml_author`.

title: Blogdown yaml considerations
description:
Hey @malcolmbarrett,

I'm still so pumped about this package after the demo last week, and I applaud your herculean effort to include blogdown yaml here. Some considerations based on my experiences working with Hugo yamls:

1. I think [yml_blogdown.R](https://github.com/rstudio-education/ymlthis/blob/master/R/yml_blogdown.R) needs an `archetype` argument that defaults to `post`. This at least matches the new post addin in blogdown, but still not perfect (i.e., the hugo future imperfect theme uses [blog instead](https://github.com/jpescador/hugo-future-imperfect/blob/master/archetypes/blog.md)- I guess the tough thing is these could be ANYTHING, they are user-defined and therefore theme dependent). If no archetypes are present (would be weird but can happen), the default is to just return only the predefined content. Which leads me to...

1. There are two types of front matter: [predefined](https://gohugo.io/content-management/front-matter/#predefined) (which you have) and [user-defined](https://gohugo.io/content-management/front-matter/#user-defined) (tougher). It would be awesome if there was a way to pull yaml options from your theme's archetypes (so if I picked `post` as the archetype, these are my yaml options from the [academic theme](https://github.com/gcushen/hugo-academic/blob/master/archetypes/post/index.md)). A few things to keep in mind here:
    - Some of these may clobber the predefined fields- you don't want duplicate `date` fields for example or you'll get an error and with lengthy yaml files the duplicate fields are hard to find (hey- enhancement idea with IDE support is to highlight duplicate yaml fields!)
    - The presence of the `""` and `[]` in the yaml values is critical to preserve for the theme to work properly
    - The `#` comments (if present) are hugely helpful but tough sometimes to assume what bit they refer to (the academic theme author leaves a blank line between the yaml "chunks")

All this leads me to thinking that perhaps what is needed is improvements to the blogdown new post addin, because it uses the archetype specified from the theme but it strips the `""`, `[]`, and `#`. 

Maybe the ymlthis package could (a) add in the predefined front matter content, (b) dump the full batch of archetype-specific yaml all at once (instead of piece by piece) since there is typically no line by line documentation present, then (c) sweep out the duplicate fields (keeping the archetype over the predefined one to preserve comments).

Anyway, sorry for burdening you with all this! Curious to hear what you think.

title: pandoc not found unlike with rmarkdown - use Rstudio Pandoc ?
description:
I got this error

``` r
ymlthis::use_pandoc_highlight_style("pygments", "test.theme")
#> Error in system2("pandoc", args = args, stdout = TRUE): '"pandoc"' not found
```

<sup>Created on 2019-08-06 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

There is indeed a check in the function
```r
stop_if_pandoc_not_installed()
```
that uses `rmarkdown::pandoc_available()` which uses `Sys.getenv("RSTUDIO_PANDOC")` in addition of pandoc in PATH. 

So this is `TRUE` on my setup because I am in RStudio so pandoc is found
``` r
rmarkdown::pandoc_available()
#> [1] TRUE
(rmarkdown:::find_pandoc())
#> $version
#> [1] '2.7.2'
#> 
#> $dir
#> [1] "C:/Program Files/RStudio/bin/pandoc"
```

I think this package should use the same mechanism and maybe use directly `rmarkdown::pandoc_exec()`. The fact that the PATH should not be modified when using Rmarkdown is a good thing.

``` r
system2(rmarkdown::pandoc_exec(), "--print-highlight-style=pygments")
```

I can help with a PR if needed.

title: Why the name filed instead of author ?
description:
I may have missed something but why by default author is set to a name field  ? 
Default field for Rmarkdown are often `date`, `title`, `author`, `output`, but no `name` field

``` r
library(ymlthis)
# add a name field but not author
yml()
#> ---
#> name: Christophe Dervieux
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> ---
yml(author = TRUE)
#> ---
#> name: Christophe Dervieux
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> ---

# do not add the author name field
"author: Christophe Dervieux\n" %>% 
  yml(author = TRUE)
#> ---
#> author: Christophe Dervieux
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> ---

# add another author field
yml() %>%
  yml_author("Christophe Dervieux")
#> ---
#> name: Christophe Dervieux
#> date: '`r format(Sys.Date())`'
#> author: Christophe Dervieux
#> ---
```

<sup>Created on 2019-08-06 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

In the [doc](https://r-lib.github.io/ymlthis/articles/yaml-overview.html), it is not clear as the example is 
```yaml
---
name: Malcolm Barrett
---
```
> In R, the equivalent structure is a list with named character vector: **list(author = "Malcolm Barrett")**. In fact, you can call this list in R Markdown using the metadata object: **metadata$author** will return the YAML in the metadata header.

Again, I may have misunderstood something here but I find it odd to have two field with a name. 
I have to add explicitly the author but the doc says 
> By default, **yml() looks for your name** (using getOption("usethis.full_name"), getOption("devtools.name"), and whoami::fullname()) and uses today's date **to use in the author** and date fields respectively

Let's note that with default pandoc template, author field can be one element string or can have name, affiliation and email elements. 

Is there something to change here ? 
Thanks.

title: Add `ymlthis::` prefix to options for .Rprofile?
description:
Hey,

Great package! I just added a few ymlthis options à la:
https://github.com/r-lib/ymlthis/blob/0642b68edc35ea4f2259b7ddf9c32dddb8de6dec/vignettes/introduction-to-ymlthis.Rmd#L243-L255

For the example options shown, you need to either prefix them (the option I went with) or attach ymlthis. The below works in `.Rprofile` on a fresh R session.
```r
   ymlthis.rmd_body = c( 
     "", 
     ymlthis::setup_chunk(), 
     "", 
     ymlthis::code_chunk( 
       library(ymlthis) 
     ) 
```

Happy to do a PR to make the change, but wanted to check in first.

title: Documentation
description:
Most functions have roxygen already, some have param descriptions, and a few have function descriptions. The chief work here is

- [x] make templates for describing yml objects, return values, etc
- [x] pull documentation for the many YAML fields (and probably clean up existing roxygen descriptions)
- [x] include roxygen family tags for `yml*_()`, `use_*()`, and for functions related to specific packages, e.g. "blogdown"
- [x] sweep for other family types (R Markdown, shiny, websites)

title: use_pandoc_template(), use_pandoc_highlight_theme()
including references in YAML
description: [it's possible to include citations directly in the YAML header](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_bibliographies_and_citations.html#inline_references) rather than e.g. `.bib`. I think there is an expected way to write it, e.g. https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/LaTeX/Bibliography_Management#biblatex. However, it might be more effort than it's worth to try and document all field options

title: rmarkdown:: not needed in output field but needed to validate
description:
`yml_output(pdf_document())` doesn't work without loading the rmarkdown package because it validates the YAML by running the function. However, output: rmarkdown::pdf_document is unnecessary and unusual. 

Specify a list of internal rmarkdown functions to switch when validating?

title: sort a few fields?
description: e.g. title, subtitle, author, date, output, then keep rest in the order specified by the user

title: color bug in print method
description:
right now the print method just finds the names of each field and highlights them. `pkgdown_template()` is good example where this fails. 

Perhaps solve by splitting with stringr and using replace rather than replace_all (will only fill in the first one). However, I think that will fail in unnamed lines (`- x`) where the argument is the name of a field somewhere else

title: site field for blogdown (and others?)
description:
blogdown takes a `site` field that seems to just be a string of the function name. If not, can use `yml_output()` approach to capture and verify

title: Warn if overriding field
description: ymlthis takes the same approach as ggplot to layering objects: if a field is named twice, the most recent is used. ggplot also warns about this. I think there should be a function `warn_if_duplicate_fields(yml_object, new_feilds)` that checks this and emits a warning
